titleEn: Poly-B Pipe Replacement in Vancouver & Metro Vancouver: 2026 Costs, Risks & What Homeowners Need to Know
titleZh: 温哥华及大温地区聚丁烯（Poly-B）管道更换完整指南（2026年版）
contentEn:
Vancouver-area homeowners with homes built between 1986 and 1997 face a hidden threat: Poly-B piping. Grey in colour with dull fitting connections, polybutylene (Poly-B) was installed in an estimated 60,000 Metro Vancouver homes before being discontinued due to failure rates linked to chlorine reactions in municipal water supplies. If your Richmond, Surrey, or Coquitlam home still has Poly-B pipes, you are sitting on an insurance and liability risk that worsens every year.

How to Know If Your Home Has Poly-B Pipes

Poly-B pipes are typically grey plastic tubing 12 to 25 mm in diameter with dull white or grey fittings using crimp or insert connections. They most commonly run through basements, crawlspaces, and inside walls. Copper manifold systems replaced Poly-B in new construction after 1997. Marked piping near your water heater, under sinks, or running along basement ceiling joists are the most visible indicators. A plumber can confirm within 30 minutes whether your home is affected.

What Happens When Poly-B Fails

Poly-B fails in two ways: micro-fractures that cause slow leaks invisible to the eye, and sudden burst failures that can release thousands of litres of water inside a home in hours. Insurance companies in BC have classified Poly-B as a high-risk condition since the early 2000s. Many BC home insurers now refuse to issue new policies on homes with documented Poly-B plumbing, and those that do charge significantly higher premiums. A single water-loss claim from a Poly-B burst can exceed $75,000 in structural remediation, making proactive replacement the cheaper option.

2026 Poly-B Replacement Cost in Vancouver and Metro Vancouver

Re-plumbing an average Vancouver single-family home with copper or PEX piping in 2026 ranges from $8,000 to $25,000 depending on the size of the home, the configuration of the existing system, and whether the work is done in stages. Supply line replacement alone — the most common failure point — typically costs $5,000 to $12,000 for a typical 2-bath single-family home. Full re-pipe including drain lines runs $15,000 to $25,000.

PEX vs Copper for Poly-B Replacement

Modern replacement piping uses either PEX (cross-linked polyethylene) or copper. PEX is the most common choice in Vancouver re-piping because it is less expensive, faster to install, and resistant to the chlorine chemistry that degraded Poly-B. Copper is preferred in cases where the home has copper fitting connections already or the homeowner prefers a material with a longer documented lifespan. PEX carries a 25-year warranty; copper carries a 50-year warranty.

Permits Required for Re-piping in Metro Vancouver

Re-piping in BC municipalities requires a building permit when the work involves modifying the supply or drain piping system. In Vancouver, Surrey, Richmond, and Coquitlam, a plumbing permit is required for any work that adds, removes, or alters piping. Cosmetic work — replacing shutoff valves, swapping a faucet, or replacing a water heater — does not require a permit in most municipalities. Opening walls to access pipe runs for a full re-pipe does require one. Reno Stars handles permit applications as part of every re-piping project at no additional charge.

What Triggers a Re-pipe vs Repair

Poly-B failures are progressive. A single pinhole leak in a basement crawlspace is a signal, not an isolated event. If you have documented evidence of two or more Poly-B leaks in the same home, insurance companies will typically require a full re-pipe as a condition of renewing or issuing coverage. Waiting for multiple failures before acting also risks water damage remediation costs that far exceed the re-pipe cost. Reno Stars offers a scoped inspection visit that documents the condition of visible Poly-B piping and provides a written re-piping scope and cost estimate — useful for both homeowner planning and insurance negotiations.
contentZh:
温哥华地区的业主注意：建于1986年至1997年间的房屋面临聚丁烯（Poly-B）管道这一隐性威胁。灰颜色的聚丁烯管道以铜或灰胶连接接头连接，据估计曾安装于大温哥华地区约60,000套房屋中，后因与城市供水中的氯产生化学反应而导致的故障率被停止使用。如果您的列治文、素里或高贵林房屋仍使用Poly-B管道，您的房屋正面临逐年恶化的保险和责任风险。

如何判断您的房屋是否有Poly-B管道

Poly-B管道通常是直径12至25毫米的灰色塑料管，接头采用压接或插入式连接，颜色暗淡发白或灰色。管道最常见于地下室、爬行空间和墙体内侧。1997年后新建房屋采用铜歧管系统替代了Poly-B。查看热水器附近、水槽下方或沿着地下室天花板托梁的管道标记，是最直观的判断方式。水管工可以在30分钟内确认您的房屋是否受影响。

Poly-B管道失效的后果

Poly-B管道以两种方式失效：导致肉眼看不见的慢漏的微裂纹，以及可在数小时内向室内释放数千升水的突然爆裂。BC省的保险公司自2000年代初已将Poly-B列为高风险状况。许多BC省房屋保险公司现在拒绝为有Poly-B管道记录的房屋承保新保单，而承保的保险公司则收取明显更高的保费。单次Poly-B爆裂导致的水损索赔，结构修复费用可超过75,000加元，使主动更换反而成为更经济的选择。

2026年温哥华及大温地区Poly-B管道更换费用

2026年，在温哥华一栋典型独栋住宅使用铜管或PEX管道重新布管，费用在8,000至25,000加元之间，具体取决于房屋面积、现有管道配置，以及是否分阶段施工。仅更换供水管道（最常见的故障点），对于典型2卫独栋住宅通常费用为5,000至12,000加元。全管道更换（含排水管）费用为15,000至25,000加元。

Reno Stars已在列治文、素里、高贵林和本拿比完成多个全面和部分管道更换项目。以下为这些已完成项目的实际合同金额。

Poly-B管道更换：PEX vs 铜管

现代更换管道使用PEX（交联聚乙烯）或铜管。PEX是大温哥华地区管道更换最常见的选择，因为成本更低、安装更快，且耐受导致Poly-B降解的氯化学物质。铜管则在对现有管道系统已采用铜接头连接的情况下，或业主偏好使用寿命更长的材料时更受青睐。PEX管道保修25年，铜管保修50年。

大温地区管道更换所需许可证

BC省各市政当局要求对涉及修改供水或排水管道系统的工程申请建筑许可证。在温哥华、素里、列治文和高贵林，任何新增、拆除或改动管道的工程均需申请管道许可证。装饰性工程（如更换阀门、换水龙头或更换热水器）在大多数市政当局无需许可证。凿开墙壁以进行管道更换的全面工程则需要申请许可证。Reno Stars在每个管道更换项目中包含许可证申请办理流程——不额外收费。

什么情况下需要全面更换 vs 局部修复

Poly-B管道失效是渐进性的。地下室爬行空间中单个针孔泄漏是一个信号，而非孤立事件。如果您的房屋有两次或以上Poly-B泄漏的记录证据，保险公司通常会将全面管道更换作为续保或出具新保单的条件。在多次失效发生后才采取行动，也面临远超更换费用的水损修复风险。Reno Stars提供管道状况检查服务，检查可见Poly-B管道状况，提供书面更换范围和成本估算——可用于业主规划和保险谈判。
